title: Strategic Talent Pipelining and Role Readiness Playbook
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's end-to-end approach for building a sustainable talent pipeline that connects hiring, structured onboarding, and early performance feedback into a single role-readiness lifecycle. The guiding principle: make hires predictable by managing inputs (role competency profiles + candidate funnel quality), outputs (time-to-readiness and performance), and transition points (handoffs & certifications).

Scope
-----
Applies to all full-time and long-term contractor hires that require multi-week onboarding and role certification across engineering, product, infra, and product-adjacent functions. Excludes short-term contractors (<30 days) and purely apprenticeship/intern rotations (those follow the internship playbook).

Key definitions
---------------
- Role Readiness Score (RRS): A numeric 0–100 measure that combines knowledge checks, ramp milestones, and manager confidence.
- Activation Sprint: A focused 7–14 day onboarding sprint with clear deliverables to validate basic operational competency.
- Hiring-to-Ramp SLA: Target elapsed time from offer acceptance to RRS >= 70. Default SLA is 45 days for engineering ICs, 30 days for product managers, and 21 days for customer-facing roles.

Principles
----------
- Gate by competency, not calendar: progression depends on demonstrated ability.
- Narrow, measurable milestones: every handoff includes acceptance criteria.
- Manager accountability: the hiring manager is the owner for role readiness; people-ops enforces cadence and tooling.
- Continuous data: capture trial metrics (time in interview stage, pass rates, RRS trajectories) to continuously improve the pipeline.

Role Readiness Score (RRS)
-------------------------
RRS is composed of three weighted pillars:
1) Operational Competency (40%) — tasks completed in Activation Sprint, checklist pass rate.
2) Technical/Domain Skills (40%) — interview scorecard points, coding/analysis challenge results, a skills assessment.
3) Manager Confidence & Integration (20%) — manager survey, teammate peer feedback.

Example scoring formula (normalized):
RRS = round( (0.40 * OpScore) + (0.40 * TechScore) + (0.20 * MgmtScore) )
Where each subscore is 0–100.

Target thresholds and actions
- RRS >= 85: Fully ramped; schedule 6-month growth plan discussion.
- RRS 70–84: Operationally capable; continue role-specific enablement and complete certification.
- RRS 50–69: Targeted remediation plan (2–4 week micro-sprint) owned by manager + mentor.
- RRS < 50: Re-evaluate fit; if persistent after remediation, escalate to People Ops for formal review.

Hiring-to-Ramp SLA and Measurement
--------------------------------
- SLA definition: number of calendar days from offer acceptance to RRS >= threshold (role-specific).
- Measurement cadence: People-ops dashboard updates daily; hiring manager confirms milestones in the LMS and signals RRS checkpoints at day 7, 21, 45.
- Escalation: If a hire is >10 days past SLA and RRS < target, an automatic review meeting is scheduled (manager, people-ops, hiring recruiter).

Process flow (intake -> pipeline -> activation -> certification)
----------------------------------------------------------------
1) Intake (owner: hiring manager + recruiter)
   - Create Role Competency Profile (RCP) with top 6 must-have skills, 3 nice-to-haves, and success metrics for month 1 / 3 / 6.
   - Attach expected Hiring-to-Ramp SLA and preferred interview panel.
2) Sourcing & Interviewing (owner: recruiter + interview panel)
   - Use standardized scorecard (see example below).
   - Maintain funnel hygiene: target 4 qualified interviews per hire.
3) Offer & Pre-boarding (owner: recruiter)
   - Share pre-boarding schedule and first-week Activation Sprint brief.
4) Activation Sprint (owner: manager + onboarding buddy)
   - Two-week focused onboarding with daily standups, shadowing, and small deliverables.
   - Complete Operational Competency checklist by day 10.
5) Role Certification (owner: manager)
   - At day 21–45, certify RRS via combined assessment (technical review + manager survey + peer feedback).

Interview scorecard (example CSV rows)
-------------------------------------
PanelMember,SkillCategory,Weight,ScoreOutOf10,Notes
HiringManager,SystemDesign,3,8,Good tradeoffs in latency/cost; follow-up on caching choices
SeniorEngineer,CodeQuality,3,7,Edge cases missing; tests absent
ProductLead,ProductSense,2,9,Clear prioritization, user empathy

Score mapping: convert ScoreOutOf10 to 0–100 by (score * 10) and multiply by Weight/totalWeight to get TechScore.

Operational Competency checklist (Activation Sprint)
---------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Account and access provisioned (IDP, Slack, internal tooling)
- [ ] Local dev environment: builds and tests run locally
- [ ] First meaningful commit merged to main (or equivalent process)
- [ ] Support rotation/triage participation scheduled (where applicable)
- [ ] Primary onboarding docs reviewed and noted in LMS
- [ ] Buddy shadowing completed for critical flows

Stakeholder responsibilities
----------------------------
- Hiring manager: craft RCP, lead Activation Sprint, certify RRS, run 1:1 onboarding check-ins twice weekly in first month.
- Recruiter: maintain funnel reporting, own offer and pre-boarding communication, confirm start logistics.
- People-ops: enforce SLA, facilitate Activation Sprint templates, maintain dashboard and run quarterly pipeline retrospective.
- Buddy (peer): daily check-ins during activation sprint, provide peer feedback survey at day 14.

Activation sprint template (two-week)
-----------------------------------
Week 0 (preboarding):
- Day -7: Send welcome packet and preboarding checklist (access, workspace setup, paperwork).
- Day -2: Schedule first-week calendar blocks (team intro, infra walkthrough, activation sprint kickoff).

Week 1: Foundations
- Day 1: Kickoff, culture & mission briefing, admin tasks, pair with buddy.
- Day 2: Environment setup, first small ticket assigned.
- Day 3: System orientation and read-through of RCP.
- Day 4: Shadow run, end-of-day demo of what was learned.
- Day 5: First commit + manager quick sync.

Week 2: Integration
- Day 6–8: Work on a 1–2 day feature/bug; cross-team touchpoints.
- Day 9: Security/operational training, runbook read + table-top exercise.
- Day 10: Activation Sprint demo + OpScore assessment.
- Day 11–14: Buffer for remediation, additional training, and final manager survey.

Onboarding milestones and acceptance criteria (text table)
--------------------------------------------------------
Milestone | Owner | Acceptance criteria | Measurement
-----------|-------|---------------------|-----------
Access & accounts provisioned | Recruiter | All core systems (IDP, ticketing, code) accessible | Confirmed checklist
First commit merged | New hire + Manager | Merge to main with code review passed | PR merged + build green
Operational participation | New hire | Participated in triage and runbook exercise | Event attendance + Log entry
RRS >= 70 | Manager | Combined scores uploaded to LMS and manager certifies | RRS recorded

Remediation & targeted coaching
--------------------------------
If RRS < 70 at certification checkpoint:
1) 7–14 day targeted remediation plan created with specific deliverables.
2) Assign mentor and schedule 3 checkpoints (day 3, day 7, day 14 of remediation).
3) If improvement < 10 RRS points after remediation, escalate to People Ops for formal next steps.

Performance & feedback integration
----------------------------------
- First 30/60/90 review templates are tied to RRS and are required inputs to calibration meetings.
- Managers must document outcomes in the performance system and set measurable objectives for month 3 and month 6.
- Calibration: The people-ops team runs a monthly new-hire calibration for hires in their first 90 days with RRS scoring and outlier detection.

Manager playbook: first 90 days (summary)
--------------------------------------
- Week 0: Prepare RCP, create Activation Sprint tickets, assign buddy.
- Week 1–2: Run Activation Sprint, daily check-ins, OpScore assessment.
- Day 14–21: Verify technical assessment and peer feedback.
- Day 21–45: Run certification, record RRS, schedule remediation if needed.
- Day 45–90: Transition to growth plan and standard performance cycle.

Metrics and dashboards
----------------------
Key metrics (tracked weekly):
- Time-to-RRS70 (median by role family)
- Activation Sprint pass rate (percent of hires completing Op checklist by day 10)
- Offer acceptance to start days (preboarding delays)
- Remediation rate (percent of hires needing a remediation plan)
- 90-day retention and early performance quartiles

Reporting cadence
- Weekly: hiring funnel health dashboard (recruiter + hiring manager)
- Monthly: new-hire calibration and SLA adherence report (people-ops)
- Quarterly: pipeline retrospective with hiring managers and recruiting leadership

Template snippets
-----------------
Example preboarding email subject:
Subject: Welcome to Redwood — preboarding and Activation Sprint details
Body: Hi <Name>, welcome! Please complete the attached preboarding checklist and confirm your start date. Your Activation Sprint kickoff is scheduled for Day 1 at 10:00am with <Manager> and <Buddy>.

Example remediation plan (bullet format):
- Goal: Reach OpScore >= 75 by day 14 of remediation
- Activities: pair-programming sessions (4 x 1h), targeted trainings (2 x 90m), practical task with acceptance criteria
- Owners: Manager (overall), Mentor (paired work), People-ops (if further support needed)

Appendix: role_readiness_config (example YAML for automation)
-----------------------------------------------------------
role: "senior-software-engineer"
hiring_to_ramp_sla_days: 45
rrs_threshold: 70
activation_sprint_days: 10
ops_checklist_items:
  - idp_access
  - dev_env_build
  - first_commit
  - buddy_shadow
  - triage_participation
